sourceCheck: Pinned Java SE 25, the current LTS release. The Oracle Support Roadmap, updated September 15, 2026, confirms that Oracle designates Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25 as LTS releases and plans Java 29 for September 2027. LTS is a vendor support designation. Java 27 is the latest feature release; Oracle lists Java 26 and 27 as non-LTS, released in March and September 2026. Oracle's language-change pages for 26 and 27 list primitive patterns as fourth and fifth previews and list no finalized language feature. Access limitation: attempts to open https://openjdk.org/projects/jdk/ and its 21/, 22/, 23/, 24/, 25/, 26/, 27/ and 28/ pages, and https://openjdk.org/jeps/431, 440, 441, 444, 456, 458, 485, 491, 506, 511, 512, 513, 507 and 465 returned HTTP 403. Consequently, the exact GA dates supplied in the prompt (25: 2025-09-16; 26: 2026-03-17; 27: 2026-09-15), the six-month project cadence, the JDK 25 'most vendors' wording and the exact 26/27 JEP lists were not independently reverified from those pages. The supplied JDK 28 snapshot reports JEP 401 Value Objects (Preview) integrated and JEP 543 Structured Concurrency proposed to target as final; those project statuses remain unverified. An official JEP 401 draft search result places its preview in Java SE 28, but does not establish integration status. Preview-status cards will remain pinned to Java 25. Oracle 25 documentation confirms finalization of sequenced collections, record patterns, pattern matching for switch and virtual threads in 21; unnamed variables and patterns and multi-file source launching in 22; stream gatherers and synchronized virtual-thread unmounting in 24; scoped values, module imports, compact source files, instance main methods and flexible constructor bodies in 25. It confirms String Templates were withdrawn from Java 23 onward. The JLS SE 25 index is dated 2025-07-29. JLS 1.5.1 requires preview enablement at compilation and execution and provides no subset selection. JLS 1.5.2 lists exactly one preview language feature: Primitive Types in Patterns, instanceof, and switch. Integer(int) in Java 25 is @Deprecated(since="9") with no forRemoval flag; 26 and 27 match, while 24 marks it for removal. Java 25 Thread omits suspend and resume; Java 26 Thread omits stop. Successfully opened https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/java-se-support-roadmap.html, https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/, and https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/index.html plus jls-1.html, jls-3.html, jls-4.html, jls-5.html, jls-6.html, jls-7.html, jls-8.html, jls-9.html, jls-10.html, jls-11.html, jls-12.html, jls-14.html, jls-15.html and jls-17.html. Under https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/language/ opened index.html, java-language-changes-release.html, pattern-matching.html, type-patterns.html, pattern-matching-instanceof.html, pattern-matching-switch.html, record-patterns.html, records.html, sealed-classes-interfaces.html, switch-expressions-statements.html, text-blocks.html, local-variable-type-inference.html, unnamed-variables-patterns.html, flexible-constructor-bodies.html, module-import-declarations.html, compact-source-files-instance-main-methods.html and preview-language-vm-features.html; their titles matched the intended Java 25 pages. Also opened https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/text-blocks/index.html; under /25/core/ opened java-collections-framework.html, creating-immutable-lists-sets-and-maps.html (title: Creating Unmodifiable Lists, Sets, and Maps), concurrency.html, virtual-threads.html and scoped-values.html; under /25/migrate/ opened significant-changes-jdk-22.html and significant-changes-jdk-24.html. Under https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/ opened java/lang/Object.html, Integer.html, String.html, StringBuilder.html, Record.html, Enum.html, Comparable.html, AutoCloseable.html, Throwable.html, Thread.html, ScopedValue.html, IO.html and doc-files/ValueBased.html; java/math/BigDecimal.html; java/util/Objects.html, Collection.html, List.html, Set.html, Map.html, SequencedCollection.html, SequencedSet.html, SequencedMap.html, SortedSet.html, ArrayList.html, HashSet.html, LinkedHashSet.html, TreeSet.html, HashMap.html, LinkedHashMap.html, TreeMap.html, Arrays.html, Collections.html, Optional.html and Comparator.html; java/util/stream/package-summary.html, Stream.html, Collectors.html and Gatherers.html; java/util/function/package-summary.html; java/util/concurrent/ExecutorService.html, Executors.html, Future.html, ConcurrentHashMap.html and Semaphore.html. API titles identified Java SE 25 & JDK 25. Comparison-only opens included the 24, 26 and 27 Integer pages, the 26 Thread page and the 26/27 language-change pages. Under https://dev.java/learn/ opened language/constructs/basics/primitive-types/, using-var/ and switch-expression/; language/constructs/numbers-strings/autoboxing/ and strings/; language/oop/classes-objects/, inheritance/overriding/, interfaces/defining-interfaces/ and records/; language/fp/pattern-matching/, generics/type-erasure/, generics/wildcards/, lambdas/functional-interfaces/ and lambdas/method-references/; language/annotations-exceptions/exceptions/catching-handling/; api/collections-and-streams/collections-framework/factory-methods/, streams/gatherers/ and streams/optionals/; api/virtual-threads/. Required refinements to the section descriptions: r2 String methods preserve the receiver but may return that same instance, so 'returning a new String' is too broad; r4 restricted constructor-prologue field assignments may use this.field, so a blanket ban on this is too broad; r11 checked exceptions also include direct Throwable subclasses outside Error and RuntimeException; r12 direct run() executes a Runnable for a platform thread, whereas direct run() on a virtual thread does nothing. The Java 25 virtual-thread guide names native methods and foreign functions as pinning causes. dev.java retains older pinning advice and outdated switch guidance; Java 25 specifications take precedence. The compact-source guide contains stale bare println examples and inaccurate print/println bullets; the IO API supplies the authoritative behavior. The switch guide's broad exhaustiveness wording needs the precise JLS 14.11.2 distinction.

cards.statement: A method's local `int n;` declaration gives `n` the default value zero.
cards.explanation: A local int variable needs definite assignment before a read; its declaration alone supplies no value.
cards.misconception: Local variables receive the same default values as fields.

cards.statement: Adding two `int` values throws ArithmeticException when the mathematical sum exceeds the `int` range.
cards.explanation: An overflowing int sum wraps within the int range; integer overflow itself raises no exception.
cards.misconception: Integer overflow raises ArithmeticException.

cards.statement: `-7 / 3` evaluates to `-2` because integer division truncates toward zero.
cards.explanation: Integer division rounds a negative quotient toward zero, giving -2 for -7 divided by 3.

cards.statement: A `char` value represents an unsigned 16-bit UTF-16 code unit.
cards.explanation: Java's char stores one UTF-16 code unit; a supplementary Unicode character occupies two such units.

cards.statement: `short s = 1; s += 1;` compiles because `+=` includes a conversion back to `short`.
cards.explanation: Compound assignment converts the addition's result back to the short variable's type.

cards.statement: `Double.NaN == Double.NaN` evaluates to `true`.
cards.explanation: Floating-point == returns false when either operand is NaN, even when both operands are Double.NaN.
cards.misconception: NaN compares equal to itself.

cards.statement: Unboxing a null Integer reference throws NullPointerException.
cards.explanation: Unboxing needs the wrapper's primitive value. A null Integer reference triggers NullPointerException during that conversion.

cards.statement: With `Integer a = 127, b = 127;`, `a == b` evaluates to `true`.
cards.explanation: The JLS guarantees identical references when the same integer constant in the range -128 to 127 is boxed.

cards.statement: `Integer.valueOf(1).equals(Long.valueOf(1))` accepts the Long as an equal numeric value.
cards.explanation: Integer.equals requires its argument to be an Integer holding the same int value. A Long argument yields false.
cards.misconception: Numeric wrappers compare equal across wrapper types.

cards.statement: Given overloads `f(long)` and `f(Integer)`, the call `f(1)` selects `f(Integer)`.
cards.explanation: f(1) selects f(long): primitive widening matches before overload resolution considers boxing.
cards.misconception: Boxing takes priority over primitive widening in overload resolution.

cards.statement: For an ArrayList<Integer> containing 1, `remove(Integer.valueOf(1))` removes its first matching element.
cards.explanation: An Integer argument selects List.remove(Object), which removes the first occurrence equal to that argument.

cards.statement: In Java 25, the Integer(int) constructor carries a deprecation marked for removal.
cards.explanation: Java 25 declares Integer(int) as @Deprecated(since="9"), with no forRemoval flag.
cards.misconception: The Integer constructor retains its earlier for-removal status in Java 25.
cards.volatilityNote: Constructor deprecation metadata may change in future Java releases.

cards.statement: Calling `replace` on a String writes the replacement characters into that String.
cards.explanation: String.replace returns its result while leaving the receiver's characters unchanged.
cards.misconception: String.replace edits its receiver in place.

cards.statement: `"tr" + "ue" == "true"` is true because the concatenation is a constant expression.
cards.explanation: The constant concatenation "tr" + "ue" denotes the interned String "true", so the references match.

cards.statement: After `String p = "tr";`, `(p + "ue") == "true"` compares the same interned String instance.
cards.explanation: Run-time concatenation with non-final p creates a new String whose reference differs from the literal "true".
cards.misconception: Run-time concatenation automatically reuses the matching interned String.

cards.statement: `final String p = "tr";` makes a local `p` usable in String constant expressions.
cards.explanation: A final String local initialized with a constant expression is a constant variable and can participate in constant expressions.

cards.statement: `"go".equals(new String("go"))` compares the identity of the String objects.
cards.explanation: String.equals compares character content. Both String objects contain "go", so this call returns true.
cards.misconception: String.equals uses reference identity.

cards.statement: A String switch matches `case "go"` when its selector is `new String("go")`.
cards.explanation: A String switch compares its selector with String case constants using String.equals, so matching text selects that case.

source.title: JLS 25 §14.11.1.2: Determining the Applicable Switch Label

cards.statement: For distinct StringBuilder objects holding "go", the call `equals` returns `false`.
cards.explanation: StringBuilder.equals checks builder identity rather than character content, so matching text leaves distinct builders unequal.

cards.statement: `"\u2003x\u2003".trim()` returns `"x"` by removing the surrounding Unicode white space.
cards.explanation: String.trim removes characters whose values are at most U+0020. The U+2003 EM SPACE characters remain around "x".
cards.misconception: String.trim removes Unicode white space such as EM SPACE.

cards.statement: The compiler requires a line terminator after a text block's opening triple quotes.
cards.explanation: A text block opening consists of triple quotes, optional horizontal white space, and a line terminator before the content.

cards.statement: A text block preserves unescaped trailing spaces at the ends of its content lines.
cards.explanation: Text block processing strips trailing white space from content lines.
cards.misconception: Ordinary trailing spaces in a text block survive into its String value.

source.title: Java SE 25 Text Blocks Programmer's Guide

cards.statement: The compiler normalizes CRLF line endings in text block source content to LF.
cards.explanation: Text block processing converts source CRLF and CR line terminators to LF before interpreting escapes.

cards.statement: In a text block, backslash followed by a line terminator inserts a newline into the String.
cards.explanation: The backslash-line-terminator escape suppresses that source line break in a text block's String value.
cards.misconception: A text block line-continuation escape preserves the source newline.

cards.statement: Object.equals compares the values of an object's fields when the class inherits that method.
cards.explanation: Inherited Object.equals returns true for two references to the same object; it does not inspect fields.
cards.misconception: Object.equals derives equality from an object's fields.

cards.statement: The equals contract specifies agreement between `a.equals(b)` and `b.equals(a)` for non-null references.
cards.explanation: Symmetry requires both directions of an equals comparison between non-null references to give the same result.

cards.statement: The equals contract makes `a` equal to `c` when `a` equals `b` and `b` equals `c`.
cards.explanation: For non-null references, equality is transitive: if a equals b and b equals c, a must equal c.

cards.statement: Under the equals contract, `x.equals(y)` may alternate results while both objects' state stays fixed.
cards.explanation: The equals contract requires repeated comparisons of the same objects to agree while equality-related information stays unchanged.
cards.misconception: equals may alternate results even when the compared state stays fixed.

cards.statement: Equal objects return matching hash codes under the hashCode contract.
cards.explanation: Objects equal according to equals must produce the same hashCode result.

cards.statement: The hashCode contract requires unequal objects to return distinct hash codes.
cards.explanation: Unequal objects may share a hash code; the hashCode contract permits collisions.
cards.misconception: A hash code uniquely identifies an unequal object.

cards.statement: The Map contract specifies stable lookup after a key changes in a way that affects equals.
cards.explanation: Changing equality-related state while an object is a Map key puts the map's behavior outside its specified guarantees.
cards.misconception: A Map specifies reliable lookup after a stored key's equality-related state changes.

cards.statement: `Objects.equals(null, null)` returns `true` while safely handling the null arguments.
cards.explanation: Objects.equals treats two null arguments as equal.

cards.statement: `Objects.hash("x")` returns the same hash code as `"x".hashCode()`.
cards.explanation: Objects.hash computes an array-style hash for its arguments, which differs from "x".hashCode() for this single argument.
cards.misconception: Objects.hash of one value reproduces that value's hashCode.

cards.statement: With distinct arrays `int[] a = {1}, b = {1};`, the call `a.equals(b)` returns `false`.
cards.explanation: An array's equals checks its reference identity; these separately created arrays are unequal despite their matching elements.

cards.statement: A naturally ordered TreeSet keeps BigDecimal values `4.0` and `4.00` as one element.
cards.explanation: BigDecimal's natural ordering treats 4.0 and 4.00 as equivalent, so a naturally ordered TreeSet retains a single element.

cards.statement: The value-based class guidance recommends equal instances as interchangeable synchronization monitors.
cards.explanation: The guidance says synchronization on value-based instances is "strongly discouraged": a program cannot guarantee exclusive monitor ownership.
cards.misconception: Equal value-based instances are suitable interchangeable locks.

cards.statement: Code in the same package can access a package-private field of an accessible class.
cards.explanation: Package access permits member access from code in the declaring class's package.

cards.statement: A subclass declaration overrides an inherited static method with the same signature.
cards.explanation: A subclass's matching static method hides the superclass method; static methods are not overridden.
cards.misconception: Static methods participate in overriding like instance methods.

cards.statement: A virtual instance method call chooses an override using the receiver's runtime class.
cards.explanation: Virtual method lookup selects an override from the receiver's runtime class hierarchy.

cards.statement: A class executes its instance field initializers before executing its superclass constructor.
cards.explanation: A class executes its instance field initializers after its superclass constructor returns.
cards.misconception: Subclass instance field initializers run before superclass construction.

source.title: JLS 25 §12.5: Creation of New Class Instances

cards.statement: A superclass-typed reference selects an accessible superclass field that its runtime class hides.
cards.explanation: Field lookup uses the expression's compile-time type, selecting the accessible superclass field.

source.title: JLS 25 §15.11.1: Field Access Using a Primary

cards.statement: `class A{void f(Object x){}} class B extends A{@Override void f(String x){}}` can compile.
cards.explanation: The subclass's f(String) overloads f(Object), so @Override makes this declaration a compile-time error.
cards.misconception: @Override accepts an overload with a different parameter type.

cards.statement: Declaring an array reference final makes assignments to its array elements compile-time errors.
cards.explanation: A final array reference cannot be reassigned, but its array elements remain assignable.
cards.misconception: final on an array reference freezes its elements.

cards.statement: An inner member class instance has an immediately enclosing instance of its outer class.
cards.explanation: A non-static member class is an inner class; its instance is associated with an instance of the enclosing class.

source.title: JLS 25 §8.1.3: Inner Classes and Enclosing Instances

cards.statement: The default constructor of a package-private class has public access.
cards.explanation: A normal class's default constructor has its class's access level; for a package-private class, that access is package access.
cards.misconception: The compiler gives each default constructor public access.

cards.statement: The compiler inserts `super()` into an empty constructor body in an ordinary subclass.
cards.explanation: An empty ordinary subclass constructor implicitly invokes the direct superclass's no-argument constructor.

cards.statement: In Java 25, a constructor prologue may assign to its class's field declared as `int x;`.
cards.explanation: A Java 25 constructor prologue permits writes to same-class fields that have no initializer, including this.field assignments.

cards.statement: Reassigning a method's reference parameter changes the reference stored in the caller's variable.
cards.explanation: A method parameter receives a copy of the argument's reference value; reassigning that parameter leaves the caller's variable unchanged.
cards.misconception: Java passes the caller's reference variable itself to the method.
